list: The official 55 trophies, as published on PlayStation (names, descriptions and grades from the Exophase / PSNProfiles listing of 2026-11-18). Guides are original writing for this entry.

trophies.guide: The platinum is the finish line, not a task of its own. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then stranger strands and activities, then collectibles and the long grinds — and this pops automatically once the other 54 trophies are in your collection. If it does not pop, check the checklist: one trophy is still outstanding, most often a grind counter such as 250 stunts or 100 WAiNK spots.
trophies.missableNote: Cannot be missed: it pops the moment the other 54 are earned.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps: Play through the story (Stage 1) and earn every story and mission trophy.
Finish the stranger strands and side missions (Stage 2).
Clear the activities, collectibles and combat trophies (Stage 3).
Use the Next-Up planner to chase the last few counters, then confirm all 54 show as earned.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn. Follow the on-screen prompts and the mission markers; there is no way to fail the trophy permanently, and replaying the mission from the pause menu also counts. Treat it as your warm-up for the checklist: open the tracker afterwards and mark it earned.
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: unmissable as long as you play the mission.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps: Start a new game and follow the opening sequence into Gone Fishing.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes once its last story mission is done. Play the main missions in order and watch the chapter card change; side activities can wait. If you are hunting efficiently, use the chapter break to clear nearby collectibles before moving on, but nothing in Chapter 1 is required for this trophy beyond finishing the chapter.
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: unmissable.

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is a straight story beat: finish its missions in order and the trophy follows. The chapter opens up more of Leonida, so it is a good moment to start the long counters — vehicles discovered and areas explored tick up naturally as you travel between missions. Do not worry about optional objectives; chapter completion only needs the missions done.

trophies.guide: Chapter 3 takes the story into Vice City proper. Keep pushing the main missions; the trophy is awarded at the chapter card, not at any single mission. By now the map is wide open, so between missions grab any WAiNK spots and meditation spots you pass — they are the two longest collectible grinds and every early one saves time later.
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: unmissable.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale. Finish its missions and the trophy pops at the chapter card. Before you push into the final mission, pause and check the missable flags in this guide — the partner trophies and the choices trophy are easiest while the story is still open and your partner is available.

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy: finish the final mission and the credits roll with this in your collection. The mission itself is the only requirement — difficulty and optional objectives do not matter. Make a manual save before starting it, because after the finale the game continues in free roam and that save is your clean jumping-off point for the Stage 3 cleanup.
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: unmissable. Make a manual save before the final mission so you can return to free roam cleanly.

Follow the markers, keep your health up with snacks or cover, and do not worry about style — completion is all that counts. If a segment goes wrong, the mission checkpoints restart you close by.

trophies.guide: The hardest trophy in the set and the whole endgame. The 100% checklist appears in the game's Progress menu once the story is done, and progress you make during the story already counts toward it. It is not a literal 100% of everything: the checklist asks for a defined set of story, side, collectible and activity items, so open it early, read exactly what it asks for, and let it steer your Stage 3 cleanup instead of guessing. Nothing on the checklist is missable, and everything can be finished in free roam after the story.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable in free roam: every checklist item stays available after the story.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps: Finish the story, then open the 100% Completion checklist in the Progress menu.
Work the checklist category by category, ticking items in this guide as you go.
Clear the longest grinds last (stunts, WAiNK spots, challenges) with the counters in this tracker.
Reach the checklist's required total; the gold trophy pops with it.

trophies.guide: Stunts are the game's jump, flight and parachute challenges, tracked in the Progress menu. Any 250 count — mix stunt jumps, under-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps however you like, and repeat nothing: each stunt location counts once. The practical approach is to work region by region from the map's stunt markers, knocking out the easy jumps first, and to keep going past 250, because the 100% checklist wants more stunts than this trophy does.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: stunts stay available in free roam.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps: Open the stunt list in the Progress menu and note the regions with the most uncompleted stunts.
Clear stunt jumps and under-bridge flights first — they are the quickest.
Track your count here; at 250 the silver trophy pops.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida's activities are the side pastimes scattered across the map — fishing, hunting, golf, shooting ranges, pool, basketball, arcade games, racing and stunts among them. Try each type at least once; the in-game Progress menu shows which activity types you have sampled, so check it rather than guessing. The story introduces several of them on its own, and working on the other activity trophies covers most of the rest, so this one usually pops without being chased.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: every activity stays open in free roam.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The shooting ranges host 42 challenges across their locations, and this trophy wants a gold medal in every one. The gold thresholds are reachable with practice: steady your aim, learn each challenge's target pattern, and retry a challenge immediately when you miss gold — retries are free and instant. Work location by location and tick each gold off in the counter below. The ranges also feed the 100% checklist, so the time is never wasted.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: ranges stay open in free roam.
trophies.name: The Shootist

Earn gold on each challenge, retrying immediately when you fall short.
Repeat at every range location until all 42 show gold; the silver trophy pops.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations around Leonida, and this trophy wants one win at each. You only need a single win per location, not every race there. Learn the racing line on your first attempt, then win on the retry — the drones handle the same way every run, so a lost race is a free practice lap. Tick each location off as you win it.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: drone races stay open in free roam.
trophies.name: Top Fun

Race it; if you lose, retry immediately with the line you just learned.

trophies.guide: Twenty different race wins: each race location counts once, so winning the same track twenty times does nothing. Leonida has far more than twenty race locations, so pick the ones that suit your driving — short circuits first — and tick each new win off here. A race you lose costs nothing but the retry, and the same car that wins one track usually wins its neighbours.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: races stay open in free roam.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is the fishing rival you meet through the story's fishing introduction. Take his challenge when it is offered and beat his catch: watch the line tension, reel steadily instead of yanking, and let the fish tire itself out. If you lose, challenge him again — the trophy only needs one win. Fishing also feeds the activity list for Master of None, so the trip is never wasted.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: the challenge can be retried.

trophies.guide: Pick any one arcade game and play it to the end. The arcade machines are found in bars and arcades around Leonida, and some games are also playable on the TV at home. You only need to finish one game once — beating every side challenge inside it is not required — so choose whichever game you enjoy most and learn its pattern over a couple of runs.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: arcade machines stay playable in free roam.

Optional character chains stay available after the story, so if a mission is not offered yet, keep playing the story and it will appear.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks are the odd jobs offered by strangers across Leonida, marked with question marks on the map. Complete eight full strands — a strand is a small chain of missions for one stranger, and a single one-off mission does not count as a strand. Check the Progress menu's stranger list to see which strands are finished, and start new ones whenever you pass a marker in free roam. They all stay available after the story, so this is a Stage 2 job, not a race.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: stranger strands stay available after the story.

trophies.guide: Randy's chain is built around delivering vehicles he asks for. Each request names a car to find and bring to his marker — scan likely cars with the WAiNK app to check whether one matches his list, then drive it back in good condition. Finish the chain's last delivery and the trophy pops. Deliveries stay available after the story, so there is no deadline pressure.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: the chain stays available after the story.

trophies.guide: Tyrone's chain of optional missions appears as the story progresses. Follow the markers in order and finish the chain's last mission for the trophy. trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida, and this trophy wants every one. Meditation spots are quiet, scenic places — check the Progress menu's collection list to see which you have found and which regions are still empty, then travel to the missing ones and meditate at each. One spot is tied to the early story: in Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning and follow her to the balcony to learn meditation. Do that scene while it is available, because it cannot be repeated after Chapter 1 ends.
trophies.missableNote: MISSABLE: the Chapter 1 meditation lesson at the house (after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the morning) cannot be repeated once Chapter 1 ends. Do it on your first playthrough.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret is the hunting contact who asks you to track down a unique animal. His request arrives by text once his strand unlocks in the story; follow the marker to the hunting grounds, track the animal with the hunting tools the game gives you, and take it down cleanly. A clean, single shot preserves the animal's condition and pays better, but the trophy only needs the hunt completed and turned in to Bret.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: Bret's strand stays available after the story.

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are scattered across Leonida in sets, and this trophy wants any three complete sets. Do not hunt cards at random: pick one set, learn where its cards sit from the map and collection menu, and finish it before starting the next — a finished set is progress you can see, while a dozen half-finished sets are not. Cards are a pure collectible grind, so they fit naturally into the Stage 3 cleanup route.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: cards stay collectible in free roam.

Complete any 3 full sets to pop the silver trophy.

trophies.guide: WAiNK is the phone app that scans the world: point it at landmarks, curiosities, sculptures, vehicles and animals and scan them. Any 100 scanned locations count, and there are far more than 100 to choose from, so make scanning a habit from the first hour — scan whatever you walk past instead of making a separate trip for it. The counter in this tracker is yours to keep; the game's own WAiNK list shows what you have already scanned.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: WAiNK spots stay scannable in free roam.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps: Open the WAiNK app on the phone and scan a nearby landmark.
Keep scanning as you travel — landmarks, sculptures, curiosities all count.
At 100 scanned locations the silver trophy pops.

trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's long list of optional feats, tracked in the Progress menu. Complete any 50 of them. Many finish on their own while you work on other trophies — driving, shooting, collecting and exploring all feed the list — so check the list late in the run and pick the easiest remaining ones instead of grinding from zero. The 100% checklist wants even more challenges, so this trophy pops on the way there.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: challenges stay completable in free roam.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

Complete any 50 to pop the trophy.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This one needs your partner beside you, so it can only be done once both characters can free-roam together. Call your partner, build a 4-star wanted level, then escape: drive out of the search area and keep going until the wanted stars clear completely — the trophy pops when you are fully clear, not when you merely break line of sight. A fast bike helps you slip through traffic, and a tunnel or back road helps you break the search. Do it before the story's final stretch, while your partner is reliably available.
trophies.missableNote: MISSABLE in practice: needs your partner free-roaming with you. Do it while both characters are available, before the final mission.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps: With your partner alongside you, build a 4-star wanted level.
Escape the search area and keep driving until the stars clear.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, staying wanted the whole time — the wanted level must never drop to zero between robberies. Plan a route of three close-together shops in advance, hit them quickly one after another, and keep moving between them. If the wanted level clears, the chain breaks and you start over. Do it while your partner is available in free roam, and bring armour for the escape after the third shop.
trophies.missableNote: MISSABLE in practice: needs your partner alongside you and a kept wanted level. Do it while both characters are available, before the final mission.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discovering a vehicle means scanning it with the WAiNK app — you do not need to drive it or own it. Stand on a busy road and scan everything that passes: cars, bikes, boats and aircraft all count toward the 100. The same habit feeds the WAiNK trophy, so the two counters climb together. Check your discovered total in the Progress menu's vehicle section.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: vehicles stay scannable in free roam.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming mode: activate it while aiming and the focus meter drains as time slows. The trophy wants five enemies downed inside one activation, so set the scene first — find a group of five enemies standing close together, top up the focus meter with food or rest, and only then trigger it. An assault rifle with full-auto fire is the practical choice: aim for the highlighted weak points and keep firing without missing, because a miss wastes the precious seconds. If the meter runs dry at four, reload the attempt and try a denser group.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: can be retried at any gang operation or shootout.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps: Find a group of at least five enemies close together.
Top up your focus meter before the fight.
Activate Combat Focus and down all five before the meter empties.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and an unscheduled departure means taking a plane that was never meant to fly you anywhere. Get onto the airfield, board one of the large passenger planes at a departure terminal, get it to the runway and take off. Fly clear of the airport and the trophy pops. Expect a wanted level on the way in — go in fast, board quickly, and do not stop to fight on the tarmac.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: the airport stays open in free roam.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps: Get onto the VCIA airfield and reach a passenger plane at a departure terminal.

Take off and fly clear of the airport to pop the trophy.

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the military tanks, and this trophy is about getting into one. The tanks are stationed at a military air base on the map's edge — approach the base, find a Rhino, climb in and drive it. The base is guarded, so expect armed resistance on the way in; the trophy pops once you are in the driver's seat and rolling. Bring a fast vehicle for the approach and do not stop to fight the whole base.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: A stealth robbery: get into a jewelry store, take the valuables and get out without any alarm or witness raising the alert. Go in quietly — use the back entrance where one exists, move slowly, avoid the staff's line of sight, and leave the way you came instead of smashing the front display. If anyone spots you, the attempt is blown: leave, lose the heat, and try another store. The trophy only counts a clean run.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: jewelry stores can be robbed again after a failed attempt.

trophies.guide: Bank vaults are the big robberies: follow a security van to its bank, slip in while the vault is open, take the cash and escape. Each robbery draws a heavy police response, so plan the escape before the entry — a fast bike parked nearby beats any plan made mid-chase. Bring your partner along where the vault holds more cash than one person can carry. Five vaults, five escapes, and the silver is yours. The same robberies feed the money trophies, so the haul is never wasted.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: bank vaults stay robbable in free roam.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks run the roads around Vice City's banks. Block one, break into its cargo hold — explosives on the rear doors are the usual method — take the cash and escape before the response arrives. The truck stops are the risky part: the crew is armed and the police arrive fast, so hit the doors quickly and be moving again within seconds. One successful robbery and escape pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Leonida is the whole state, and this trophy wants all 52 of its areas visited. The map's fog is your checklist: every blacked-out patch is an area you have not been to yet. The fastest way to clear it is by air — take a plane or helicopter and fly over each fogged region until the map fills in. On the ground, driving the highways between missions clears most of it naturally, so check the map late in the run and fly over only what is left.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: every area stays visitable in free roam.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run illegal operations across Leonida — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling dens and the like — and this trophy wants one robbery from each gang's turf. Operations are marked on the map when you get near them, and the Progress menu's gang section shows which gangs you have hit. Work gang by gang rather than at random: finish one gang's operation, check it off, and move to the next gang's territory. The same robberies feed the 100% checklist.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is the beachfront strip in Vice City, and the trophy is exactly what it sounds like: have a cocktail somewhere with a view of it. Walk the beachfront until you find a bar or venue with a seafront view, order a drink and enjoy it. No verified step-by-step route has been published by the cited sources yet, so this guide does not invent a specific venue — the description itself is the whole clue, and any beachfront bar with a view qualifies.
trophies.missableNote: Unmissable: Ocean Beach bars stay open in free roam.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: This one is a deliberate homage: take a car from a vehicle showroom and drive it straight out through the showroom window. Get inside the showroom, get into a display car, and floor it through the glass instead of using the door. The trophy pops on the smash-through, so the escape afterwards is just for style. Any showroom with a street-facing window works — pick one with a clear road outside so you do not stall on the glass.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The Kolt & Associates bowling alley is a place, not just a pastime: go there and bowl. The trophy's wording — follow-through — is about completing the act, so play a full game and finish it rather than leaving halfway. The alley is also tied to a gang operation, so expect company if you visit during that strand; the bowling itself is a normal activity and the trophy pops when the game is done.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about the partnership itself: build your duo's standing until the pair is widely known. The practical reading of the description is that it tracks the partnership's public profile — the activities you do together, the missions you finish as a pair, and the time you spend free-roaming side by side. No single mission triggers it, so keep playing together and check the trophy list's progress counter to see it climb. It pops once the partnership's appeal crosses the threshold.

trophies.guide: Leonida keeps score of your choices: PSN tracks a count up to 500, and this trophy pops when the counter fills. Choices are the decisions the game offers — in conversations, in missions, in how you handle a job — and each one nudges the count. There is no right answer to chase; make the choices as they come and the count climbs on its own. Turn on the game's choice notifications if they exist in the settings, so you can see each decision land. Late in the run, check the counter in the trophy list and finish the remaining decisions in free roam.
trophies.missableNote: MISSABLE in practice: choices are one-time decisions. Make choices whenever the game offers them, and do not skip decision prompts.

trophies.guide: The description is a riddle, not an instruction: succeed at something on the second try. The honest position of this guide is that no cited source has published a verified trigger for this trophy yet — the description alone is the clue. The practical approach is to keep failing forward: whenever a challenge, race or activity offers a retry, take it, because the trophy most likely watches for a success that follows a failure. Do not force it; play normally, retry what you lose, and it should surface on its own.

trophies.guide: Another riddle trophy: the description reads like a reaction to something strange in the world. The honest position is that no cited source has published a verified trigger yet, so this guide will not invent a location or a sequence. Wander Leonida's odd corners, especially at night and off the highways, and it will find you.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by: strike someone with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The practical method is a motorcycle — ride alongside a pedestrian or enemy and swing as you pass, so the bike's speed does the work and your swing only has to connect. Aim for a lone target on a quiet road rather than a crowd, because the trophy wants the knock-down, not a fight. One clean hit from a moving vehicle pops it.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked bills are the cash from robberies that cannot be spent as-is — they have to be laundered through your contacts. Rob banks, vaults and armored trucks, then take the marked bills to a fence or contact who washes them. The $250,000 is cumulative across the whole game, not one job, so every laundered dollar counts. The bank vaults pay the biggest sums, so this trophy climbs fastest once those are open; early on, smaller robberies still add up.

trophies.guide: The simplest money trophy: spend $100,000 in total across Leonida's shops. Every purchase counts — guns, car mods, clothes, tattoos, food — and the total is cumulative, so normal play already moves the needle. The fastest way to finish it off is the expensive end: weapon upgrades and car modifications eat thousands per visit. If you are short late in the run, buy the priciest mods you can and the counter will close quickly.

trophies.guide: Garages are bought through the game's property app on the phone, and this trophy wants all 8 purchasable ones. They are not cheap, so the practical route is to save the purchases for the late game, when bank vaults and laundered bills have filled your wallet. Buy them one at a time as money allows, and check the property list to see which are still unowned. Garages also store the cars you need for other trophies, so the money is an investment, not a sink.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles so they can be delivered to you anywhere. Steal or buy a vehicle, open the app and register it — each registration counts once per vehicle, so ten different vehicles are needed. Cheap cars and bikes are the efficient choice: register the low-end ones you pass on the street instead of rare or expensive rides. You need garage space for the registered vehicles, so buy a garage or two first if the app refuses a registration.
